ui_bugs.issue: After a SUCCESSFUL submit(), only `onScheduled?.()` is called — the modal does NOT self-close and there is no explicit `onClose()` in the success path. Whether the modal closes therefore depends on the parent wiring; on the current /shop/biz_demo_bar the modal stays visible after a real successful create (verified: ITER188 event IS persisted + appears on Social > Live, but the scheduler overlay remains open). Recommend calling `onClose?.()` after `onScheduled?.()` OR having the parent's onScheduled close the modal itself. Reference: /app/frontend/src/pages/bar/BarOwnerScheduler.jsx:53-54

action_items: (LOW) BarOwnerScheduler.jsx: after successful submit, also call onClose (or have the parent's onScheduled close the modal) — currently the overlay stays open after a real successful create so the user must manually X out even though the event was scheduled.

(Optional) Add a lightweight toast/link on both web scheduler and mobile scheduler after submit that jumps the user to Social > Live > Upcoming so they can immediately see their newly scheduled event.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/bar_games.py: still has duplicate __all__ declarations flagged in iter185/186/187 — cosmetic only, second one wins.

BarOwnerScheduler.jsx: `addFromCatalog` filters out empty-title rows BEFORE appending — so tapping a catalog card when both empty product rows are visible collapses them into a single populated row (the two empty rows disappear). Users looking for a 3rd manual row must click 'Add product' after. Not a bug, just UX-different from what a naive user might expect. Consider preserving all rows and only replacing rows whose title equals the picked product name to avoid deduping.

DrinkPerks.jsx share(): swallows share errors silently (catch {}). Since navigator.share on desktop Chrome typically doesn't exist, the code falls through to navigator.clipboard.writeText + a success toast — but if clipboard write itself throws (e.g. non-secure context, permissions), the user gets no error feedback. Consider showing a toast.error on the clipboard-branch failure path.
